title: Risk profile, riskometer and horizon
objectives: Separate risk capacity (what finances can afford) from risk tolerance (what a client can stomach).
Read SEBI's six-level riskometer and match horizon to asset type.
body_md:
A risk profile has two halves: capacity, what the client's finances can afford to lose, and tolerance, what falls they can live through without selling. Every scheme carries SEBI's riskometer label — Low, Low to Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High, Very High — and most equity funds show Very High. Investment horizon is how long the money can stay invested: equity suits 5+ years, liquid funds suit weeks to months.

| Term | Plain meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Risk profile | How much risk a client can take (capacity) and is comfortable taking (tolerance) | A 28-year-old with stable income vs a 68-year-old living on interest |
| Riskometer | SEBI's six-level risk label on every scheme: Low, Low to Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High, Very High | Most equity funds show "Very High" |
| Investment horizon | How long the money can stay invested | Equity for 5+ years; liquid funds for weeks to months |
| Volatility | How much and how often returns swing up and down | A small-cap fund can fall 30% in a year and rise 50% the next |

> **Talk-track:** “Return is what you hope for; risk is what you might live through on the way. Let's check you can live through the bumpy part.”
example: A 28-year-old with stable income and a 68-year-old living on interest need very different risk profiles, even for the same amount.
say: The riskometer labels the fund; suitability matches the fund to the client.
Equity is for money you will not need for 5+ years.
never: Most equity funds are low risk because they are regulated.
Horizon doesn't matter if the fund is good.
